ResearchDossier.topic: the ring finger vein to the heart is a myth
ResearchDossier.summary: Before medical science understood circulation, people believed a vein ran directly from the fourth finger of the left hand to the heart, the vena amoris ('vein of love'). The 1662 Book of Common Prayer put the wedding ring on the fourth finger of the woman's left hand. Today the ring is generally worn on the left hand in the former British Empire (UK, US, Canada, Australia), but on the right hand in some Orthodox and a few Catholic European countries, including Russia, Germany, Greece and Poland.
ResearchDossier.angle: The vein of love was never there.

Script.headline: Your Ring Finger Has No Love Vein
Script.cta: Follow for more things hiding in plain sight.

lines.text: There's no special vein running from your ring finger to your heart.
People once believed there was. They even named it. Vena amoris. The vein of love.
It was a belief from before anyone understood how blood actually circulates.
In 1662, England's Book of Common Prayer put the wedding ring on the fourth finger of the left hand.
That's still the custom in the UK, the US, Canada and Australia.
But in Germany, Russia, Greece and Poland, the wedding ring usually goes on the right hand.
So in Berlin, the vein of love would be on the wrong side.
